touch_decoder_swap.scope: Cross decoder and already captured first-slot contexts. All 128 committed queries from seed A, per-arm actual generated prefixes; no labels or optimization. Contexts come from different generated trajectories, so this localizes decoder versus upstream input, not a matched-song-time causal estimate.

touch_same_input_history_replay.scope: 16 equally spaced first-slot queries from the same generated prefix trajectory. Identical candidate, audio inputs, condition, history and state for weight swaps; explicit route-removal interventions are labelled. Fixed cached lens/planner outputs from the configuration arm for all variants. No sampling or training.

symbolic_mask_probe.scope: Four fixed high-Touch generated queries; 16 input-mask draws each, fixed cached audio. Internal neural dropout disabled, only top-level symbolic/history/ledger masking varies. This is a forward distribution probe, not training evidence.

architecture_findings: Trace reproduces original chart hashes: Touch drift exists in raw model logits before sampling.
Changing only the final decoder on captured contexts barely changes Touch probabilities.
Identical-input replay gives about .584 Touch for both trained arms; no single swapped upstream module removes it.
Removing token history alone leaves .399 Touch; removing token history and per-pad timing leaves .226.
Route removal is a diagnostic intervention, not a validated production fix or musical target.
Random history masking does not eliminate the high-Touch response on the four fixed difficult queries.
Short recovery corrects a training gap but has not established robustness to long self-generated configurations.
configuration_recovery_verdict: Training connection verified, quality not accepted: repetition fell but Touch increased to 52.71%/46.27%. Experimental, opt-in, unchanged live training. Neither sparse default cadence nor long-run benefit established.
